reading.body:
The three leading open-source frameworks for voice and service agents have accumulated just over 40,000 combined GitHub stars, with no single project holding more than 38 percent of that total, suggesting the space has not yet converged on a dominant standard.

Pipecat, the LiveKit agents framework, and TEN-framework are all written in Python, all actively maintained as of the data date, and all positioned around real-time voice interaction. The closeness of their star counts, roughly 15,000, 14,000, and 11,000, points to genuine competition rather than a settled hierarchy. Each carries a different licence, BSD-2-Clause, Apache-2.0, and a custom licence respectively, which matters for organizations evaluating integration constraints.

Real-time voice inference is among the more compute-intensive consumer AI workloads because latency requirements are strict and audio streams are continuous. These frameworks sit at the application layer and do not themselves reveal anything about the underlying infrastructure costs, the data centers running the models they call, or the power draw those data centers require. The data covers three repositories on one platform at one point in time, and absence from this list should not be read as absence from the market.
